title: Differential expression of proteins in hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells lacking the Cullin-5 protein
projectDescription: Cullin proteins are scaffolds that coordinate assembly of cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin (Ub) ligases (CRL), complexes that control post-translational ubiquitin modification and degradation of cellular proteins. Cullin-5 (Cul5) coordinates assembly of CRL complexes containing the RING E3 ligase Rbx1/2, the adapter proteins Elongins B and C, and a Suppressor of Cytokine Signalling (SOCS) box-containing substrate recognition protein. To explore potential roles for Cul5, we generated mice lacking Cul5 in the in hematopoietic system. Analyses included biological and molecular studies including proteomic analysis of differential expression of proteins in primary purified hematopoietic stem/progenitor (LSK) cells lacking Cul5.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Samples were prepared for LC-MS/MS analysis using USP3 protocol as outlined previously. Briefly, cells were lysed in 5% SDS lysis buffer using 10 mM Tris (2-Carboxyethyl) phosphine (TCEP) and 40 mM 2-chloracetamide (2-CAA) for 10 min at 95 °C. Acid hydrolysis of DNA was performed immediately after using TFA (final concentration 1%), and quenched using 1M Tris and pH-verified (pH 8). Lysates were then incubated with 20 μL of magnetic PureCube Carboxy agarose beads (Cube Biotech) (pre-washed three times in MilliQ water) and acetonitrile (ACN, 70% v/v) for 20 min at RT using the ThermoMixer C (Eppendorf) shaking at 400 rpm. Samples were placed on a magnetic rack, supernatant removed, and three 200 μL washes performed: twice with 70% ethanol, and one with neat acetonitrile (ACN). After washing, all traces of solvent were evaporated using a CentriVap (Labconco), and digestion buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8) was added to the beads containing Lys-C (Wako, 129-02541) and SOLu-Trypsin (Sigma Aldrich, EMS0004) each at a 1:50 enzyme to protein ratio, and digestion performed for 1 h at 37 °C with shaking at 400 rpm. Digests were desalted using in-house C18 stage tips containing 2 plugs as previously described, vacuum centrifuged to dryness, and peptides reconstituted in 5 μL 0.1% formic acid and 2% ACN in preparation for LC-MS/MS. Peptides (3 µL) were separated by reverse-phase chromatography on a C18 fused silica column (inner diameter 75 µm, OD 360 µm × 15 cm length, 1.6 µm C18 beads) packed into an emitter tip (IonOpticks), using a custom nano-flow HPLC (Thermo Ultimate 300 RSLC Nano-LC with a PAL systems CTC autosampler). The HPLC was coupled to a timsTOF Pro (Bruker) equipped with a CaptiveSpray source. Peptides were loaded directly onto the column at a constant flow rate of 400 nL/min with buffer A (99.9% Milli-Q water, 0.1% FA) and eluted with a 30-min linear gradient from 2 to 34% buffer B (99.9% ACN, 0.1% FA). The timsTOF Pro (Bruker) was operated in diaPASEF mode using Compass Hystar 5.1. The settings on the TIMS analyzer were as follows: Lock Duty Cycle to 100% with equal accumulation and ramp times of 100 ms, and 1/K0 Start 0.6 V.·/cm2 End 1.6 V·s/cm2, Capillary Voltage 1400V, Dry Gas 3 l/min, Dry Temp 180°C.  Methods were set up using the instrument firmware (timsTOF control 2.0.18.0) for data-independent isolation of multiple precursor windows within a single TIMS scan. The method included two windows in each diaPASEF scan, with window placement overlapping the diagonal scan line for doubly and triply charged peptides in the m/z – ion mobility plane across 16 × 25 m/z precursor isolation windows (resulting in 32 windows) defined from m/z 400 to 1,200, with 1 Da overlap, with CID collision energy ramped stepwise from 20 eV at 0.8 V·s/cm2 to 59eV at 1.3 V·s/cm2.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA-NN 1.8 was used for searching of timsTOF diaPASEF .d files. The option for library-free search was enabled, and data were searched against reviewed sequences from the mouse Uniprot Reference Proteome (downloaded May 2021). The search was set to trypsin specificity, peptide length of 7-30 residues, cysteine carbidomethylation as a fixed modification, variable modifications set to n-terminal protein acetylation and oxidation of methionine, and the maximum number of missed cleavages at 1. In addition, the maximum mass accuracy was set to 10 ppm for both MS1 and MS2 spectra and the quantification strategy to robust LC (high precision). Match between runs (MBR) was enabled, and all other settings left as default including filtering outputs at a precursor q-value < 1%. Data processing and analysis of DIA-NN outputs were performed using R software (version 4.2.1). Protein groups taken for statistical analysis had PG.Q.Value > 0.01, were derived from proteotypic peptides only, and had PG.MaxLFQ recorded in at minimum 40% of replicates in at least one condition. Total of 6,694 proteins were included in the analysis. For these proteins, the PG.MaxLFQ intensities were log2-transformed, and missing values were imputed by applying Missing Not At Random (v2-MNAR) method implemented in msImpute R-package (v. 1.3.3). Data were normalized using RUVIIIC method (v. 1.0.19). This was achieved by utilising 3,766 proteins as negative controls, which were chosen empirically.
